CHAPTER 1: THE LONG WALK OUT.

▶ 0m 09s

The storm had finally broken against the petrified canopy, leaving the morning shrouded in a bruised, exhausted quiet. Squad 907 trudged out through the arena's winding canyon, their boots dragging through churned mud and splintered basalt needles, the sharp tang of ozone still clinging to the back of every throat.

▶ 0m 29s

Overhead, mounted high upon the iron observation towers, a stadium intercom speaker crackled through the mist, broadcasting a looping automated recording across the ruined trees: "Power has been restored. Please come to the exit of the arena. You have succeeded! If you are hearing this and still breathing, you have definitely succeeded! For the rest, please... we will find you. Make fires or smoke signals if you need help.".

▶ 0m 54s

Ignatius wiped a smear of soot from his jaw, a slow grin cutting through the grime on his face.

▶ 1m 01s

"You hear that, guys?"

▶ 1m 02s

he called back over his shoulder.

▶ 1m 04s

"We passed.".

▶ 1m 06s

Lomi tilted his woolen flat cap back against the pale sky and let out a short, ragged laugh.

▶ 1m 11s

"Yeah. I guess they weren't kidding that it was dangerous."

▶ 1m 15s

He shook his head, the reality catching in his throat.

▶ 1m 18s

"Holy shit. I was not expecting that.".

▶ 1m 20s

"Yeah. They really unleashed a little bit of stuff on us back there," Ignatius agreed, rolling his sore shoulder.

▶ 1m 28s

"They definitely trusted us in our abilities.".

▶ 1m 31s

"I know it wasn't intentional on the proctors' part," Lomi said, glancing back at the shredded tree line where the corrupted felines and storm raptors had ambushed them in the dark, "but clearly they had monsters at the ready to point downhill. This was no joke.".

▶ 1m 48s

"Hey, we passed," Ignatius said, warming to the thought.

▶ 1m 52s

"Hopefully I passed that written exam, too. We'll find out about that later, I'm sure.".

▶ 1m 57s

Lomi snorted with dry amusement.

▶ 2m 00s

"You don't need a written test if you impress the right people. That's all I'm saying. Hopefully all the impressive shit we pulled out in the open is enough to outweigh anything that happened in the trees. And I'm pretty sure that you being here means that you passed that test.".

▶ 2m 14s

Ignatius paused, his grin fading slightly as he turned the night over in his mind.

▶ 2m 20s

"We did almost die. I'm not sure I'm registering that correctly yet, but... we didn't. And that's good.".

▶ 2m 27s

They walked in silence for several paces, the strange relief of survival settling into their bones. Then Ignatius jerked his chin toward the massive, dark shape moving steadily through the underbrush ahead of them.

▶ 2m 41s

"Hey—what is with that weird turtle, Britt?".

▶ 2m 44s

Britt didn't answer. Her sharp green eyes remained locked forward, her gaze utterly fixed on the lumbering mass of the spirit tortoise ahead, entirely ignoring Ignatius's subtle dig. Her long dreadlocks of living root shifted against her grey tunic as she marched in silent, unblinking concentration, completely zoned in on the rhythmic plodding of its shell. No one was getting through her focus right now.

▶ 3m 13s

Ahead of them, Mwaza-Kasa moved with slow, unyielding momentum. The ancient spirit tortoise didn't pause, didn't glance back, and took the absolute straightest line the terrain allowed—cutting directly through dense brush toward the roaring river ahead, wholly indifferent to their stamina or how they planned to follow. It simply possessed a direction and belonged to it.

▶ 3m 38s

Ignatius glanced at Britt, waiting for an answer, but got nothing back except the steady rhythm of her strides. Shrugging, he turned instead to the dazed pixie tucked securely beneath Britt's arm.

▶ 3m 50s

"Pip," Ignatius asked, leaning in, "are you okay?".

▶ 3m 55s

The question snapped Pip right out of her shell-shocked reverie. Her oversized eyes went wide, and she squirmed in Britt's grip, exploding with frantic questions.

▶ 4m 06s

"Yeah, wait, that IS a good question. Britt, Aggie, what IS with that turtle?!"

▶ 4m 11s

Pip shouted, gesturing wildly back toward the trees.

▶ 4m 14s

"I got thrown into some sort of weird dream or something! Like a whole mental forest—".

▶ 4m 19s

Before the little pixie could finish, deep, rhythmic thuds vibrated up through the wet earth.

▶ 4m 25s

THOOM. THOOM. THOOM.

▶ 4m 29s

Heavy, booming footfalls came crashing through the petrified brush like a prehistoric beast on the hunt. Pip barely had time to let out a startled squeak before a thick emerald vine shot out from the foliage, snapped tight around her ankle, and violently yanked her clean off Britt's shoulder, yeeting her backward into the green shadows.

▶ 4m 49s

A quarter-second later, Bramble burst out of the trees, holding Pip securely by both shoulders. The towering plant-kin's wooden face warred visibly between wanting to throttle the tiny pixie and weeping with overwhelming relief, and he began berating her faster than anyone had ever heard him speak.

▶ 5m 09s

"Pip! Why did you have to go for the snacks?!"

▶ 5m 12s

Bramble scolded, his voice vibrating with frantic urgency.

▶ 5m 16s

"Pip, bad idea! Very bad idea, Pip!".

▶ 5m 21s

Behind them drifted Saffron, quiet and composed, the pale scholar they recognized from old Academy study circles where she had spent hours silently sketching in the corner.

▶ 5m 33s

Bramble skidded to a halt before Squad 907, clutching Pip against his wooden chest. He looked the squad over with solemn gratitude.

▶ 5m 42s

"Thank you," Bramble said earnestly, "for keeping stupid Pip alive.".

▶ 5m 48s

"I'm not stupid!"

▶ 5m 50s

Pip protested, flailing her tiny arms indignantly.

▶ 5m 54s

"That bird was stupid!".

▶ 5m 55s

"Hush, Pip," Bramble commanded, smoothly extending a leafy vine to wrap neatly around her mouth.

▶ 6m 02s

"Your time for speaking and eating is suspended for the indefinite future."

▶ 6m 08s

He wound a leafy vine across her lips, then bound her tightly against his torso, caging her safely within his woven branches.

▶ 6m 17s

"You're welcome," Ignatius said with a broad grin.

▶ 6m 21s

Lomi watched the vine maneuver with open admiration.

▶ 6m 25s

"I didn't realize that was an option," he muttered.

▶ 6m 28s

"Wow. We could have used that an hour ago.".

Bramble looked at them, his leafy brow relaxing a bit after finding Pip safe.

▶ 6m 46s

He glanced ahead toward the riverbank, noticing the Spirit Tortoise sliding toward the current.

▶ 6m 52s

Ignatious seeing his gaze, halfway explained "We're kind of in the middle of something, so we have to keep going. You can come too, though. Are you leaving?"

▶ 7m 02s

Bramble, took a quick look at Saffron, who just shrugged and nodded, Thanks you Ignatious we will join. Which was it out? "Follow the turtle, dude," Ignatius laughed, pointing toward the lumbering shell ahead.

▶ 7m 16s

Together, they broke through the final thicket of petrified oaks and emerged onto the muddy banks of the surging canyon river. Without slowing for a single breath, the colossal tortoise waddled straight off the ledge and dropped into the churning water with a heavy splash, disappearing beneath the foam before resurfacing to swim powerfully downstream.

▶ 7m 37s

The river ran wide, deep, and bitterly cold, swollen with runoff from the night's unnatural tempest. The ancient Spirit Tortoise was already knifing effortlessly through the center current, its broad shell parting the dark water without hesitation.

▶ 7m 53s

Iggy reached the bank first. Without breaking stride, the little dirt-kin creature tucked his wool trench coat tight around his chest and dropped straight into the churning current with a muted splash, paddling stubbornly alongside the tortoise's wake.

▶ 8m 09s

Ignatius arrived at the muddy embankment and didn't even slow down. Gathering the inner heat of his hearth-fire, he stepped straight off the ledge and continued walking out over open air, his boots gliding effortlessly a hand's breadth above the roaring surface.

▶ 8m 25s

"I'm not even flying at this point," Ignatius said with a proud grin, watching the foaming rapids rush harmlessly beneath the soles of his boots.

▶ 8m 35s

"I'm just walking above the water.".

▶ 8m 38s

Lomi jogged to the bank, looked down at the freezing rapids, looked over at Iggy and Aggie swimming, and then eyed Ignatius casually strolling across the river as if it were a paved avenue in Harmony.

▶ 8m 53s

"Uh... do you have any extra carrying capacity, buddy?"

▶ 8m 57s

Lomi called out.

▶ 8m 58s

Ignatius glanced back, rolling his neck and doing the quick mental math of a frame running on fumes after a night of relentless combat.

▶ 9m 07s

"I can carry one person, it will just take a bit of effort" Ignatius decided.

▶ 9m 12s

"I think I can grab you, hop on my back.".

▶ 9m 14s

"All right, let's go, buddy!"

▶ 9m 16s

Lomi shouted.

▶ 9m 17s

Without waiting for further deliberation, Lomi leaped off the embankment and planted himself squarely across Ignatius's shoulders, locking his arms around his friend's neck with the utter confidence of a mechanic trusting a well-built rig.

▶ 9m 32s

The fire-kin grunted loudly as the sudden weight slammed into him, his boots dipping inches toward the icy foam before his hearth-spark flared, steadying them both in mid-air.

▶ 9m 44s

"Oh god!"

▶ 9m 45s

Ignatius wheezed, straining to maintain altitude.

▶ 9m 48s

"You're much heavier than you look! You are not small!".

▶ 9m 52s

"I'm small but dense," Lomi said serenely, adjusting his flat cap and settling in comfortably.

▶ 9m 59s

"That's what people tell me.".

▶ 10m 02s

"Dense is definitely the word," Ignatius groaned, sweat beading across his forehead as he resumed his walking motion through the air, carrying Lomi across the wide expanse of river.

▶ 10m 14s

Beside them in the water, Aggie swam with smooth, practiced strokes, her white hair trailing in the foam as she kept pace with the tortoise.

▶ 10m 24s

They reached the midpoint of the crossing when a deafening crash echoed from the upstream banks.

▶ 10m 30s

KAA-SPLASH! Ignatius and Lomi twisted around to look back over their shoulders.

▶ 10m 36s

Their makeshift wooden raft—the one they had lashed together from petrified branches during their tree ordeal hours earlier—came sailing out of the forest canopy and slammed violently into the river. Standing tall upon the deck was Bramble. The plant-kin planted his massive feet against the logs, gave the tree line a triumphant thumbs-up, and scooped Saffron and Pip aboard before catching the central current.

▶ 11m 03s

▶ 11m 21s

The raft spun smoothly around the river bend, carrying them all toward the wide basin docks where the arena gates opened to the morning sun.

Chapter 2: Basin Docks

▶ 11m 31s
▶ 11m 31s

CHAPTER 2: BASIN DOCKS.

▶ 11m 35s

The exit of the Apex Arena opened onto a sprawling expanse of mud, stone docks, and white canvas tents that looked less like a staging ground and more like an emergency field hospital.

▶ 11m 47s

Rows upon rows of wooden cots stretched across the trampled basin. Cadets lay in every condition of physical ruin—some shivering uncontrollably under woolen blankets, others groaning as proctors bound splints around shattered limbs, and far too many lying motionless beneath plain grey canvas tarps, the breath gone from their chests. Academy doctors and volunteer attendants sprinted between the rows with medical kits and glowing resonance crystals. Near a larger command pavilion, a somber knot of captains spoke in hushed, urgent tones; the grim murmur drifting through the camp was that at least one or two veteran captains had died plunging into the corrupted sectors to drag surviving cadets out of the slaughter.

▶ 12m 37s

Ignatius stepped off the riverbank and came to an abrupt, staggering halt.

▶ 12m 41s

The easy humor that had carried him out of the canyon—the swagger of a cadet thinking we survived, this was all kind of a wild adventure—evaporated the instant his eyes found the silent rows of covered bodies. The color drained completely from his soot-smudged face.

"Oh..."

"Oh, fuck.".

Prologue & Title

SESSION 12: Momentum is Life.

Chapter 1: The Long Walk Out

CHAPTER 1: THE LONG WALK OUT.

The storm had finally broken against the petrified canopy, leaving the morning shrouded in a bruised, exhausted quiet. Squad 907 trudged out through the arena's winding canyon, their boots dragging through churned mud and splintered basalt needles, the sharp tang of ozone still clinging to the back of every throat.

Overhead, mounted high upon the iron observation towers, a stadium intercom speaker crackled through the mist, broadcasting a looping automated recording across the ruined trees: "Power has been restored. Please come to the exit of the arena. You have succeeded! If you are hearing this and still breathing, you have definitely succeeded! For the rest, please... we will find you. Make fires or smoke signals if you need help.".

Ignatius wiped a smear of soot from his jaw, a slow grin cutting through the grime on his face.

"You hear that, guys?"

he called back over his shoulder.

"We passed.".

Lomi tilted his woolen flat cap back against the pale sky and let out a short, ragged laugh.

"Yeah. I guess they weren't kidding that it was dangerous."

He shook his head, the reality catching in his throat.

"Holy shit. I was not expecting that.".

"Yeah. They really unleashed a little bit of stuff on us back there," Ignatius agreed, rolling his sore shoulder.

"They definitely trusted us in our abilities.".

"I know it wasn't intentional on the proctors' part," Lomi said, glancing back at the shredded tree line where the corrupted felines and storm raptors had ambushed them in the dark, "but clearly they had monsters at the ready to point downhill. This was no joke.".

"Hey, we passed," Ignatius said, warming to the thought.

"Hopefully I passed that written exam, too. We'll find out about that later, I'm sure.".

Lomi snorted with dry amusement.

"You don't need a written test if you impress the right people. That's all I'm saying. Hopefully all the impressive shit we pulled out in the open is enough to outweigh anything that happened in the trees. And I'm pretty sure that you being here means that you passed that test.".

Ignatius paused, his grin fading slightly as he turned the night over in his mind.

"We did almost die. I'm not sure I'm registering that correctly yet, but... we didn't. And that's good.".

They walked in silence for several paces, the strange relief of survival settling into their bones. Then Ignatius jerked his chin toward the massive, dark shape moving steadily through the underbrush ahead of them.

"Hey—what is with that weird turtle, Britt?".

Britt didn't answer. Her sharp green eyes remained locked forward, her gaze utterly fixed on the lumbering mass of the spirit tortoise ahead, entirely ignoring Ignatius's subtle dig. Her long dreadlocks of living root shifted against her grey tunic as she marched in silent, unblinking concentration, completely zoned in on the rhythmic plodding of its shell. No one was getting through her focus right now.

Ahead of them, Mwaza-Kasa moved with slow, unyielding momentum. The ancient spirit tortoise didn't pause, didn't glance back, and took the absolute straightest line the terrain allowed—cutting directly through dense brush toward the roaring river ahead, wholly indifferent to their stamina or how they planned to follow. It simply possessed a direction and belonged to it.

Ignatius glanced at Britt, waiting for an answer, but got nothing back except the steady rhythm of her strides. Shrugging, he turned instead to the dazed pixie tucked securely beneath Britt's arm.

"Pip," Ignatius asked, leaning in, "are you okay?".

The question snapped Pip right out of her shell-shocked reverie. Her oversized eyes went wide, and she squirmed in Britt's grip, exploding with frantic questions.

"Yeah, wait, that IS a good question. Britt, Aggie, what IS with that turtle?!"

Pip shouted, gesturing wildly back toward the trees.

"I got thrown into some sort of weird dream or something! Like a whole mental forest—".

Before the little pixie could finish, deep, rhythmic thuds vibrated up through the wet earth.

THOOM. THOOM. THOOM.

Heavy, booming footfalls came crashing through the petrified brush like a prehistoric beast on the hunt. Pip barely had time to let out a startled squeak before a thick emerald vine shot out from the foliage, snapped tight around her ankle, and violently yanked her clean off Britt's shoulder, yeeting her backward into the green shadows.

A quarter-second later, Bramble burst out of the trees, holding Pip securely by both shoulders. The towering plant-kin's wooden face warred visibly between wanting to throttle the tiny pixie and weeping with overwhelming relief, and he began berating her faster than anyone had ever heard him speak.

"Pip! Why did you have to go for the snacks?!"

Bramble scolded, his voice vibrating with frantic urgency.

"Pip, bad idea! Very bad idea, Pip!".

Behind them drifted Saffron, quiet and composed, the pale scholar they recognized from old Academy study circles where she had spent hours silently sketching in the corner.

Bramble skidded to a halt before Squad 907, clutching Pip against his wooden chest. He looked the squad over with solemn gratitude.

"Thank you," Bramble said earnestly, "for keeping stupid Pip alive.".

"I'm not stupid!"

Pip protested, flailing her tiny arms indignantly.

"That bird was stupid!".

"Hush, Pip," Bramble commanded, smoothly extending a leafy vine to wrap neatly around her mouth.

"Your time for speaking and eating is suspended for the indefinite future."

He wound a leafy vine across her lips, then bound her tightly against his torso, caging her safely within his woven branches.

"You're welcome," Ignatius said with a broad grin.

Lomi watched the vine maneuver with open admiration.

"I didn't realize that was an option," he muttered.

"Wow. We could have used that an hour ago.".

"Seriously... we could have used that trick the whole time," Ignatius agreed, laughing.

Bramble looked at them, his leafy brow relaxing a bit after finding Pip safe.

"So... you all survived too. Thank you again."

He glanced ahead toward the riverbank, noticing the Spirit Tortoise sliding toward the current.

Ignatious seeing his gaze, halfway explained "We're kind of in the middle of something, so we have to keep going. You can come too, though. Are you leaving?"

Bramble, took a quick look at Saffron, who just shrugged and nodded, Thanks you Ignatious we will join. Which was it out? "Follow the turtle, dude," Ignatius laughed, pointing toward the lumbering shell ahead.

Together, they broke through the final thicket of petrified oaks and emerged onto the muddy banks of the surging canyon river. Without slowing for a single breath, the colossal tortoise waddled straight off the ledge and dropped into the churning water with a heavy splash, disappearing beneath the foam before resurfacing to swim powerfully downstream.

The river ran wide, deep, and bitterly cold, swollen with runoff from the night's unnatural tempest. The ancient Spirit Tortoise was already knifing effortlessly through the center current, its broad shell parting the dark water without hesitation.

Iggy reached the bank first. Without breaking stride, the little dirt-kin creature tucked his wool trench coat tight around his chest and dropped straight into the churning current with a muted splash, paddling stubbornly alongside the tortoise's wake.

Ignatius arrived at the muddy embankment and didn't even slow down. Gathering the inner heat of his hearth-fire, he stepped straight off the ledge and continued walking out over open air, his boots gliding effortlessly a hand's breadth above the roaring surface.

"I'm not even flying at this point," Ignatius said with a proud grin, watching the foaming rapids rush harmlessly beneath the soles of his boots.

"I'm just walking above the water.".

Lomi jogged to the bank, looked down at the freezing rapids, looked over at Iggy and Aggie swimming, and then eyed Ignatius casually strolling across the river as if it were a paved avenue in Harmony.

"Uh... do you have any extra carrying capacity, buddy?"

Lomi called out.

Ignatius glanced back, rolling his neck and doing the quick mental math of a frame running on fumes after a night of relentless combat.

"I can carry one person, it will just take a bit of effort" Ignatius decided.

"I think I can grab you, hop on my back.".

"All right, let's go, buddy!"

Lomi shouted.

Without waiting for further deliberation, Lomi leaped off the embankment and planted himself squarely across Ignatius's shoulders, locking his arms around his friend's neck with the utter confidence of a mechanic trusting a well-built rig.

The fire-kin grunted loudly as the sudden weight slammed into him, his boots dipping inches toward the icy foam before his hearth-spark flared, steadying them both in mid-air.

"Oh god!"

Ignatius wheezed, straining to maintain altitude.

"You're much heavier than you look! You are not small!".

"I'm small but dense," Lomi said serenely, adjusting his flat cap and settling in comfortably.

"That's what people tell me.".

"Dense is definitely the word," Ignatius groaned, sweat beading across his forehead as he resumed his walking motion through the air, carrying Lomi across the wide expanse of river.

Beside them in the water, Aggie swam with smooth, practiced strokes, her white hair trailing in the foam as she kept pace with the tortoise.

They reached the midpoint of the crossing when a deafening crash echoed from the upstream banks.

KAA-SPLASH! Ignatius and Lomi twisted around to look back over their shoulders.

Their makeshift wooden raft—the one they had lashed together from petrified branches during their tree ordeal hours earlier—came sailing out of the forest canopy and slammed violently into the river. Standing tall upon the deck was Bramble. The plant-kin planted his massive feet against the logs, gave the tree line a triumphant thumbs-up, and scooped Saffron and Pip aboard before catching the central current.

The current seized the raft and hurtled it downstream with astonishing speed, effortlessly pacing and then overtaking the swimmers. As Bramble shot past Aggie and Britt, he cupped a hand to his mouth and shouted cheerfully across the water: "Thank you for the raft! Very good construction!".

The raft spun smoothly around the river bend, carrying them all toward the wide basin docks where the arena gates opened to the morning sun.

Chapter 2: Basin Docks

CHAPTER 2: BASIN DOCKS.

The exit of the Apex Arena opened onto a sprawling expanse of mud, stone docks, and white canvas tents that looked less like a staging ground and more like an emergency field hospital.

Rows upon rows of wooden cots stretched across the trampled basin. Cadets lay in every condition of physical ruin—some shivering uncontrollably under woolen blankets, others groaning as proctors bound splints around shattered limbs, and far too many lying motionless beneath plain grey canvas tarps, the breath gone from their chests. Academy doctors and volunteer attendants sprinted between the rows with medical kits and glowing resonance crystals. Near a larger command pavilion, a somber knot of captains spoke in hushed, urgent tones; the grim murmur drifting through the camp was that at least one or two veteran captains had died plunging into the corrupted sectors to drag surviving cadets out of the slaughter.

Ignatius stepped off the riverbank and came to an abrupt, staggering halt.

The easy humor that had carried him out of the canyon—the swagger of a cadet thinking we survived, this was all kind of a wild adventure—evaporated the instant his eyes found the silent rows of covered bodies. The color drained completely from his soot-smudged face.

"Oh..."

Ignatius whispered, his voice cracking on the syllable.

"Oh, fuck.".

Lomi stepped up beside him, reading the rigid tension locking Ignatius's jaw.

"I didn't think it would be this bad...because we managed it so easily," Lomi said quietly.

"Yeah. Because for us, it was a walk in the park," Ignatius said, his voice hollow and thin.

Lomi leaned in close, his tone grim.

"Damn... this really was not what they planned, huh?".

"No, dude," Ignatius muttered, staring out over the sea of wounded.

"This is... I mean, this is real. Even in combat, it always felt like a test before. It never felt real. This is the first time it's felt real to me."

His gaze darted anxiously toward the tarps, dreading what he might recognize.

"Are any of them... do you see anyone we knew?".

As the squad picked their way through the crowded aisles, Mwaza-Kasa glided forward with impossible, silent grace. The Spirit Tortoise moved in a perfectly straight line through the chaos, never touching a single person, gliding smoothly past staggered cadets on crutches and rushing attendants without a whisper of friction.

Nearby, a couple of injured cadets stared in bewilderment as the ancient beast drifted past.

"What is this beast doing here?"

one bystander muttered, turning to ask a nurse—only to blink and frown, the memory of the question vanishing from his mind the moment he looked away from the shell.

Lomi raised an eyebrow, watching the strange effect ripple through the crowd.

"Interesting.".

Beside them, Iggy had stopped walking.

The little dirt-kin creature had grown completely silent. His oversized copper goggles fogged slightly at the rims as he looked down the long line of motionless cots. He reached into the pockets of his heavy trench coat, pulling out several smooth, dark basalt stones. Moving solemnly from cot to cot, Iggy gently placed a basalt pebble upon the head, the heart, and the feet of each fallen cadet—a quiet funeral rite to ground their departed spirits back to the ancient bedrock of the world.

Pip, finally getting relased by Bramble upon entering the makeshift camp, followed immediately in Iggy's footsteps. The scene affected even her chipper attitude as she said nothing, and simply focused on carrying her massive sack of provisions slung over her tiny shoulder, every time Iggy placed a grounding stone upon a cot, Pip reached in, snapped off a warm, fresh biscuit, and gently pressed it into the hands of the shivering survivors lying beside them.

"It's the little things, I suppose."

Lomi murmured, watching the strange pair work their way down the aisle.

Ahead, near the medical supply tent, Aggie caught sight of a familiar figure and paused.

Kale, the eccentric student artisan who had crafted their experimental speaking stones, was sitting slumped on an upturned crate, his skin ghastly pale and his hands shaking. Hovering protectively over him was Val, whose eyes were bloodshot and raw with grief. Behind Val stood two cots draped in heavy tarps.

Peeking out from beneath the edge of one canvas sheet were the bent wire spectacles of Finch—Lomi's fierce Academy rival who had refused to share notes and hoarded market intel. Beneath the other tarp lay the bright blonde hair of the cadet from the potato arena.

Aggie stepped toward Val, her white hair and red-spotted mushroom shell catching the pale morning light. Remembering their previous philosophical debate about death—how the Mizizi viewed mortality as a natural return to soil and fungal renewal, while outsiders saw only tragedy—she approached with earnest sympathy.

Ignatius winced, leaning toward Britt.

"I feel like the ideology of the Mizizi is not going to go over very well right now," he whispered under his breath.

"Aggie is about to learn some hard lessons about social cues.".

"They're just different social cues!"

Britt hissed back defensively, crossing her arms.

"It's culture shock, Ignatius. Leave her alone.".

"It's called the growing pains of becoming one with Harmony," Ignatius muttered back with a dry shrug.

Aggie stopped before the cot, looking softly at Val's bloodshot eyes.

"I am sorry for your loss," she offered carefully, her voice hesitant as she tested the unfamiliar Harmony phrasing.

"I... I think I am are saying that right? But, I want you to know that it is not for nothing.".

Val looked up, his jaw clenching as he struggled between raw grief and frustration. He looked down at the tarps covering his friends, his voice tight and trembling.

"Then what is all of this for?"

Val asked bitterly, his fists clenching at his sides.

"I don't... I don't have that answer right now. I just have a feeling" Aggie replied back. Val didn't reply as he turned back to Kale, who was heavily injured on the cot nearby and grabbed his hand to wait with him.

From behind their tent, the voice of Valerius Sterling echoed across the makeshift camp, informing the outside world of the chaos that occured last night in Apex Arena.

"And we are BACK! Power is finally restored across Vumbua! Valerius Sterling here, coming to you live from the recovered Ops center of the Apex Arena—and while our technicians were frantically kicking the resonators back to life, reports have been flooding in from every sector in Harmony about strange little power blips. People are already calling it The Night of Embers—well, at least I am. Remember listeners, if that catches on: you heard it here first!"[rapid-fire, theatrical].

"Now, for our listeners who were eagerly tuned into the Academy’s baseline field survival trial in the Apex Arena: let me tell you... it did NOT go according to the brochure! The Academy’s official intent was to test our new cadets' raw survival instincts in a controlled environment. Simulating a crash landing in the wilderness with zero preparation time, scraps were scattered across the canyon floor, and a tiny, heavily monitored trickle of low-threat beasts was to be let through the perimeter gates to give the Captains a good chance to see the first-years in action.".

"Cadets were given fair warning to evacuate if they couldn't handle the heat. About a quarter of them took the hatch! But that still left thirty-five thousand eager candidates who stayed inside to test themselves against the challenge Vumbua had in store.".

"And what a show it was! We saw high-speed chases, zero-sum brawls over raw sulfur caches, improvised glider rigs, trench-digging, deep diving—every insane form of transport and salvage you can imagine! All setting up for what was supposed to be a textbook crash-landing survival exercise... which brings us to the part where the sky fell down and things got a bit more... realistic than planned. I have with me Vumbua harmonics expert Professor Kante to give us an idea of what the blazes happened last night!".

"Thank you, Valerius. You see, the main grid capacitors were ramped up to increase resonance resistance and dampen repulsor output for the beast-entry phase; however, when the umber crystal resistors were cycled back down, the planned replacement resonance failed to materialize. This triggered a systemic harmonic desynchronization across the Panda 5 cell array, as demand surged over supply, resulting in a total localized drop of the sector barrier.".

"Uh-huh. I'll be honest, listeners, I may need you to tell me what that means, because I’ll tell ya—I haven't got the foggiest!".

"Bottom line, Valerius? There was a temporary lapse in the amount of resonance required to run the Vumbua shield.".

"...Well, that sounds... scary. What does this mean for the regular Harmony citizen? Are we in danger of these repeating?".

"For now, it will mean very little. Large resonance consumers like Resonance Race Arenas will need to carefully monitor any cycling or consider more continuous draw.

But for the average citizen, you will not experience anything different. Citizens need not worry—I have great faith in our faculty. Vumbua has accelerated the Ventures. They will find the answers to this! I am particularly excited about what Professor Ink has in mind, but I should not say any more here. Rest assured, Vumbua will move forward.".

"Well, you certainly are a comfort and a bit of a tease, Professor! In any case, thank you for translating for the layman here. We look forward to reporting on what happens next!".

"Now... on a much more somber note. It is now painfully clear that when that barrier dropped, the aetheric beast horde outside didn't care about trial rules.

Not every candidate made it out of the trap we built for them. Official casualty numbers are still being tallied by Dean Vane’s office, but... we are all holding our breath and praying at least half made it through this ordeal. It is a devastating blow for the Academy, for the parents, and for the future of our adventuring class.".

"We lost seasoned veterans who held the gantry lines. Stalwarts like Sarge of the Harbor Guard, who held his post until the final civilian transports cleared the central docks, and who is even now being honored with a twenty-one-gun naval broadside by the Ironclad battleship in the bay.".

"Yet if there is one dark, silver lining to emerge from the embers today... The cadets who walked out of that clearing this morning aren't just students anymore. They are hardened survivors—more ready to face the raw, unmapped Wilderness than anyone who has come before them. The Academy has recognized this by accelerating the Proving Ventures, and I am certain these survivors will have no trouble finding a Captain eager to take them on.".

"To those who fell: we honor your sacrifice. To those who survived: carry the fire forward. Because in the face of the tempest, only one absolute truth remains: ...Momentum is Life.".

"This is Valerius Sterling—signing off.

Chapter 3: What The Shields Dropped

CHAPTER 3: WHAT THE SHIELDS DROPPED.

Lomi kept one eye on Squad 907's steady march, tracking the lumbering shell of the Spirit Tortoise as it glided between the triage rows. Weaving through the crowded medical aisles like a mechanic reading a damaged engine ledger, he searched the exhausted crowd for familiar faces from his harbor prep shifts.

Near a water distribution rig, he spotted the firefighter crew he had coordinated with before the drop. At the center of the squad stood Raphael, his broad face smeared with soot and his canvas coat torn at the shoulder.

When Raphael turned and saw Lomi approaching, a look of overwhelming relief washed over the firefighter's tired features. He stepped forward and gripped Lomi's shoulder in a bone-jarring grasp.

"Lomi! Good to see you, man," Raphael exhaled, his voice hoarse from smoke.

"I'm glad you made it through. It was brutal out there. I don't know what the hell happened.".

"Yeah, seems like it," Lomi said quietly, his eyes sweeping across the rows of wounded cadets.

"I mean... look at this place.".

Raphael scrubbed a heavy hand down his soot-streaked face. His sentences came out in clipped, ragged bursts.

"Listen... all I know is that the proctors were just trying to let a few minor aether beasts through the barrier. A controlled simulation. But the grid collapsed—and they let in the whole lot.".

"Yeah, I figured it wasn't intentional," Lomi nodded.

"When we got swarmed in the trees, I knew something had broken. But man... I didn't think it was going to go this bad.".

"It's bad, Lomi," Raphael said darkly, shaking his head.

"You're going to have to find someone a lot smarter than me to figure out what went wrong with the core.".

"I know," Lomi replied.

"That's why I'm searching for answers right now. Maybe someone closer to the faculty source.".

Raphael glanced toward the dark canopy of the petrified forest, his jaw tightening with lingering dread.

"It was even worse than we could have anticipated. Sure, there are always a few rogue aether beasts prowling outside the resonance perimeter, but this? This wasn't stray wildlife. This was an invasion.".

"Yeah," Lomi agreed solemnly.

"There have always been rumors about beasts gathering outside the barrier, but that swarm... that was insane.".

"I don't know what's coming next," Raphael said, clasping Lomi's arm, "but I guess that's why we have you out here. You're going to go figure it out for us.".

"I'll do my best," Lomi promised.

"In the meantime, I guess we're gonna help out with sorting out the mess here and helping where we can.".

"Listen, buddy," Raphael replied firmly.

"If you need anything, my crew is here for you. But right now, let us handle the triage. This mess here is our problem. You go solve the big one.".

"Understood," Lomi said.

Raphael gave him a solid slap on the back.

"We're counting on you, buddy.".

Hearing their conversation, Kale coughed weakly from his place on the cot beside Val and Aggie. The eccentric student artisan leaned up on one elbow, his face deathly pale, and reached toward his belt - pushing back Val who tried to restraing his movements to keep him from hurting himself worse.

"Lomi..."

Kale rasped, his voice trembling with exhaustion.

"Do you still have those communication stones?".

Lomi stepped over to the cot, pulling the polished crystal apparatus from his vest pocket.

"Yeah. At least one of them.".

"And I have the other one here" , Aggie added, from her place behind Val.

"Good," Kale coughed, taking the stone with shaking fingers. He pulled a small tuning crystal from his pouch, slotted it into the brass housing, and tapped the facets until a soft, harmonic chime resonated from the core.

"This is working now. I gave matching stones to some of the faculty proctors before the chaos started. They're using the frequency to coordinate.".

Val hovered beside the cot, pressing a cup of fresh water into Kale's hands.

"Take it easy, Kale. Don't strain yourself.".

Kale took a small sip and looked up at Lomi.

"The proctors dropped the perimeter shield for the trial, but the generator didn't have enough reserve resonance to reignite the barrier, which forced the existing array to burn out tryign to support the full field. Professor Kante was given one of these stones. If you find another faculty unit, you can patch through to him. He might know more about the resonance decay.".

"Professor Kante," Lomi repeated, nodding with keen interest.

"That's exactly who I was hoping to reach. Iggy says he's a genius.".

Kale held up his own speaking crystal, offering a faint, tired smile.

"I thought you might be in the thcik of what happens next. Good luck, Lomi. I'll be listening on the channel too.".

Lomi gave Kale a reassuring nod, pocketed the tuned stone, and turned back to rejoin the squad's march.

Chapter 4: No One Saw A Flare

CHAPTER 4: NO ONE SAW A FLARE.

Squad 907 was trailing the Spirit Tortoise along the basin beach when a sudden flash of vibrant electric-blue hair swept across Britt's vision.

Before Britt could raise her hands, she was enveloped in a fierce, crushing embrace that smelled faintly of sweet river reeds and canyon silt.

"Britt!"

Rill cried out, squeezing her sister with breathless intensity.

"I've been asking everywhere! No one saw a flare—not a single person! Did you not use it?!".

Britt blinked in sudden bewilderment, her stomach dropping into her boots. She looked over at Ignatius, who was jogging up alongside Lomi and Aggie to rejoin the group.

"Did we... did we have a flare?"

Britt asked softly, a sheepish flush rising on her cheeks.

"Oh shoot.".

Ignatius threw his hands up in a placating gesture, embers flickering at his cuffs.

"Well, look," Ignatius offered defensively.

"The idea was that we would fire the flare if we ever got overwhelmed. But once we were in the thick of it, we were kind of... whelmed, but never really got over-whelmed. We were just surviving! So we just might have completely forgotten the flare existed.".

Rill pulled back, staring at the two of them with wide, incredulous eyes.

"You're an idiot," Rill muttered, shaking her head in disbelief before a grin broke through her exhaustion.

"You're complete idiots—and you're brilliant, because you actually survived with your full squad intact! Not many teams can say that right now, the odds were terrible!".

Britt gestured toward Ignatius with a proud grin.

"Well, you have to know that Natty over here crafted a perfect fire Lazizi out of thin air, and it really, really helped.".

Rill raised an eyebrow, crossing her arms.

"I've never really understood how those things are useful in hunting, to be completely honest, but that sounds pretty cool.".

"And I don't know who said you can't herd wild felines," Ignatius added with a proud swagger, "because she definitely herded some cats.".

Britt smiled, then grabbed Rill's sleeve and pointed toward the lumbering form plodding steadily across the sand ahead of them.

"Rill... do you see the tortoise in front of us? Can you see that too?".

Rill turned, following Britt's finger toward the massive creature. Her eyes went wide.

"Whoa... I mean, yeah. What is that?".

"What does it look like to you?"

Britt replied with intensity.

Rill stared at the glowing lichen veins pulsing along the dark carapace. The color drained from her face as ancient clan lore surged back into her memory.

"Mwaza-Kasa..."

Rill whispered, using the sacred dialect of the elders.

"I... I recognize that as something I was taught to avoid at all possible costs.

Why is it here? Should that even be outside the grove?!".

"Exactly," Britt said firmly.

"That's why we're following it.".

Rill's expression hardened with sudden, frantic urgency. She grabbed Britt by the wrist, pulling her toward the northern pier.

"Okay, it is even more important that I get you to Professor Ink right now! Please, come with me!".

"Where are we going?"

Britt asked, stumbling slightly as Rill dragged her across the sand.

"Look over there," Rill said, pointing toward a colossal, four-legged mechanical walker perched near the harbor docks, its steel plating bearing a painted quill sigil.

"Professor Ink is up in her walker! This is crazy—this is part of her entire theory about the resonance decay!".

Ignatius jogged up beside them.

"Maybe we split up," Ignatius proposed.

"That way some of us go to the professor, and the rest of us keep following the god turtle so we don't lose its trail.".

Lomi nodded in agreement.

"Hey, and here's some great news—if the god turtle does anything crazy, we still have that flare!".

"That's why we saved it," Britt said with a smirk.

"I'll go with whoever follows the god turtle," Ignatius offered.

"If something happens, I can fly back and find the walker.".

"Wait," Lomi called out to Rill.

"Is Professor Kante up there in the walker?".

"No," Rill answered over her shoulder, "but we have the communication stones!".

Ignatius clapped his hands, trying to coordinate the split.

"All right, Aggie, Britt—which one of you wants to follow the god turtle?".

Rill looked at Britt.

"Britt, I think you really need come to. I think I might know something about that fungal rash spreading on your skin.".

Britt grimaced, glancing back at the tortoise's steady stride.

"Yeah... it's a hard sell to leave this turtle, honestly. But you're right, I'll go to the professor. I do need to figure out what is up with this thing.".

Ignatius nodded, then pointed between Britt and Aggie, squinting in confusion.

"All right... so Britt follows the turtle, and Aggie goes to the walker?".

Britt frowned.

"Wait, am I following the god turtle or is Aggie?".

"Sorry, Aggie," Ignatius muttered, rubbing the back of his neck.

"Sorry. You two look identical to me right now.".

Across the circle, Pip gasped in utter scandal.

"Have you never seen a mushroom turtle before?!"

Pip squeaked.

"That's so rude!".

Before Ignatius could apologize, Pip leapt into the air and smacked him squarely across the nose with both tiny hands.

"Natty is not dealing with loss well," Lomi sighed, shaking his head.

"No, I do not deal with loss well at all," Ignatius admitted sheepishly, holding his sore nose.

"I apologize. Clearly you are both different colors. Aggie, seems like you're with me. Let's get going.".

With the plan finalized, Squad 907 split their forces: Ignatius, Iggy, and Aggie remained on the trail of Mwaza-Kasa, while Lomi and Britt sprinted across the docks behind Rill toward the towering walker.

Chapter 5: The Walker

CHAPTER 5: THE WALKER.

Rill darted through the crowded harbor camp with the agile grace of a river fish cutting upstream. Lomi and Britt sprinted behind her, their eyes locked on the vibrant flash of her electric-blue hair as canvas tents and rushing medics blurred past.

Out of the corner of his eye, Lomi caught sight of a deeply painful scene: a few tents down, Lucky was hunched over a cot draped in heavy grey canvas, his broad shoulders heaving in silent, agonizing grief. Lucky did not see him pass. Lomi hesitated for a split second, his chest tightening—forced to make an instant choice between peeling away to comfort his grieving crewmate or staying locked on Britt's heels.

"I need to stay with Britt," Lomi muttered under his breath, clenching his fists and pushing forward.

They arrived at the base of the colossal four-legged walker. Unlike the brutish, heavy iron mining rigs of the deep harbor, this machine was remarkably lean and elegant—an arachnid marvel of articulated brass joints, reinforced struts, and streamlined copper plating. A lower entry hatch stood open, with an iron rung ladder extending down to the sand.

Rill scrambled up the ladder two rungs at a time, paused beneath the hatch to beckon them inside, and vanished into the interior. Lomi and Britt climbed rapidly behind her, ascending level after level through the machine: passing a cramped crew bunk module, a sparkling biological laboratory filled with glowing glass alembics, an operations command center with acoustic dials, and finally emerging into an airy observation lounge fitted with panoramic glass windows and steering levers.

Standing at the forward console was Professor Ink—a poised, sharp-featured elven scholar dressed in a tailored black vest, her dark raven hair bound in a precise silver clasp.

Rill burst into the cockpit, words spilling from her lips in a breathless, frantic torrent.

"Professor! Professor! You have to listen—there is something unbelievable happening! In tens of thousands of years, the elders told us that no Spirit Tortoise has ever left its grove, and now one is right out there, walking through the forest in a perfectly straight line! It completely defies the resonance decay!".

Professor Ink raised a calming hand, a faint, measured smile touching her lips.

"Calm, Rill. Breathe. Speak slower and more clearly.".

"You got this, breathe" Britt said softly, as Rill finally took a deep, shuddering breath.

"Professor, this is one of my two sisters from the Mizizi clan I told you about," Rill said, gesturing toward Britt, "This is Britt, who came with me, and Aggie is following the Mwaza Kasa right now.".

Professor Ink stepped forward, extending a gloved hand toward Britt.

"It is a pleasure to meet you," she began, then glanced out the observation glass toward the triage camp below.

"Well... perhaps not under these tragic circumstances."

Sensing Britt's hesitation, Ink smoothly shifted her posture and offered the traditional Mizizi fist-bump instead. Britt returned the gesture with a nod of respect.

Ink got straight to the core of the crisis.

"I will need more information on what you think is so urgent, Rill - but this is exaclty the reason I have decided to commission your squad to guide my expedition into the deep Mizizi forest. What occurred in the arena tonight is unprecedented, and I suspect it is tied directly to the resonance failure of the ancestral network. We will depart aboard Elijah—" she gestured to the humming steel deck beneath their feet "—the high-speed walker I designed to traverse the petrified canopy faster than any standard convoy. Would you be willing to come with me? I think I will need your understeand of the forest and it's lore to make any progress on my theory.".

"Yeah," Britt answered without hesitation.

"Half our friends are already heading toward the grove right now. So, yes.

Let's go.".

"Excellent," Professor Ink replied.

"We will rendezvous at the northern basin perimeter in one hour to board. You may bring up to ten companions—that is the operational limit for Elijah's life-support systems."

She turned toward her assistant.

"Now, Rill—let us pull in Professor Kante so he can help make sense if what you have seen.".

Lomi stepped toward the comms table, tapping the crystal apparatus in his coat.

"That works out cleanly. I was hoping we could get lggy and the professors patched in together.".

Professor Ink, nodding her permission as Lomi pulled out his device, called out over the stone, "Professor Kante, please respond.".

After a heartbeat of rustling papers, Professor Kante's intellectual, resonant voice filled the cockpit.

"I am here.

Together, Rill and Professor Ink filled in the Harmonics expert on the events of the last day, but Britt stayed mostly quiet feeling uncertain whether she shoudl add more information to the debrief.

Hmm that is quite a lot.. One moment... I am reviewing the energy telemetry. After hearing this, I feel even more confident of our working hypothesis is that the Mizizi clan has been operating under deeply repressed ancestral knowledge.

Whatever the elders taught their youth has formed an ideological block against the network's connection.".

Kante paused, his tone taking on a reflective, scholarly weight.

"Consider the historical precedent of the Ash-Blood clan. They too lived in complete isolation, terrified of taking their volcanic flames beyond the mountain rim, until someone capable of genuine cross-clan resonance bridged the gap.

What happened tonight was not random. The Spirit Tortoise's emergence indicates the ancestral web is demanding connection. Britt, can you tell us more about what this Mwaza Kasa means to the Mizizi?".

Britt stepped toward the crystal stone, her arms crossed defensively. She remained deeply wary of outside scholars and Academy motives.

"Look... all I know is that our sacred tortoise has left the grove, and we need to follow it back immediately. That's all we have.".

Kante's voice answered gently through the speaker.

"I understand your reluctance, Britt. But in the coming seventy-two hours, we must work together to move past this fear of the unknown. We need the knowledge you carry, and you need the technical reach of our walkers.".

Britt met Professor Ink's steady gaze across the console.

"When I have reason to trust you," Britt said firmly, "I will share what I know. In my own time.".

"Fair enough," Professor Ink agreed with a solemn nod.

"One hour. Prepare your squad.".

Chapter 6: Sparks In The Triage

CHAPTER 6: SPARKS IN THE TRIAGE.

Down on the basin beach, as Britt's transmission crackled away over the speaking stone, the group trailing the Spirit Tortoise witnessed the ancient creature do something completely unexpected.

Mwaza-Kasa slowed its unyielding march, stopped, and turned its massive head around for the very first time.

The tortoise's glowing golden-teal eyes met Aggie's gaze. Then, with deliberate slowness, its head pivoted toward a nearby medical cot where an slightly dissheveled but otherwise uninjured girl with a wild shock of electric-purple hair was sitting propped against the pillows. Ignatius recognized the tempest cadet immediately.

The Spirit Tortoise looked from Zephyr to Aggie, back to Zephyr, and then settled into the sand, tucking its heavy limbs beneath its shell to wait in patient, motionless silence. Britt and Ignatious looked at each other for a moment.

Shrugging, Ignatious went over to where Zephyr was squinting into the morning glare, rubbing her temple with a gloved hand.

Ignatius crouched down beside the cot, a wide grin spreading across his face.

"Hey, Zephyr! How are you feeling?".

Zephyr rolled her shoulders, testing the stiffness in her neck.

"Pretty cool," she said casually.

"Pretty cool day."

She tilted her head, studying the embers flickering at Ignatius's cuffs.

"Why are you looking at me like that? Is there something about what I am saying you find strange? Or do you just like the electricity between us?".

"No, no," Ignatius laughed, before meeting her eyes, "I'm just really glad to see you're alive and okay!".

Lomi, walking past with a stack of clean bandages, threw his hands up in sheer disbelief.

"Not the time!"

Lomi hissed.

"Read the room, man!".

"Yeah, read the room!"

Pip echoed from behind, glaring at Ignatius with wide, scandalized eyes.

"There are literally dead people all around us!".

Ignatius flushed, his flames flaring with sheepish embarrassment, but he couldn't help pushing back.

"I'm just relieved to see that she's okay!"

he stammered, before turning back to Zephyr with an awkward, lopsided smirk.

"I mean... clearly you're fine. That's good to know. But I guess some could say... some could say there might be a flame between us.".

Zephyr smirked, blue static dancing along her fingertips.

"Maybe after the lightning strikes, flames can come.".

"I'm all up for a little electric fire," Ignatius fired back with a chuckle.

Zephyr swung her legs over the side of the cot, a spark of electric pride crackling through her hair.

"HAH! You interest me," she decided, pointing a gloved finger at his chest.

"I will follow you now. Where are we going?".

"We've been following the god turtle," Ignatius said, gesturing toward Mwaza-Kasa.

"Pretty cool," Zephyr replied, sounding only mildly impressed. Then her eyes flashed with predatory excitement.

"Did you kill many beasts last night?".

Ignatius hesitated, rubbing his chin.

"I mean... I'm not sure how many we actually killed versus how many we just threw off the tree canopy without dying.".

Zephyr grinned fiercely and reached beneath her tunic, pulling out a heavy necklace strung with gruesome hunting souvenirs: three jagged teeth from a dagger-shark, two hooked claws from a bobcat, and, hanging proudly at the center, a large, iridescent feather from a storm raptor.

"I had a very successful night," Zephyr declared proudly, running her thumb across the raptor feather.

"My clan will be so proud.".

Ignatius's competitive streak flared instantly. He stood up straight, crossing his arms.

"Well, I did kill one of the raptors! I flew straight at it and smashed it right out of the sky with my hammer! And then another one came at us, and that was a whole ordeal.".

Zephyr arched an eyebrow in mock skepticism.

"Two raptors? One raptor was enough to slaughter every idiot the proctors assigned to my squad. My entire party died."

She gave an indifferent shrug.

"I never really liked them anyway. They kept trying to recruit me to stay and study 'clan connection'—told me that was the reason I was drawn to the Academy in the first place.".

Ignatius looked at her, tilting his head.

"What about the little girl who was your friend? The one who was constantly taking care of you?".

"Oh, you're referring to that silly Rill, right?"

Zephyr asked, waving a dismissive hand.

"Yeah, yeah... she was always obsessed with learning, taking notes, and writing every little thing down. That is really not my favorite thing to do.".

"I see," Ignatius laughed.

"They kept trying to recruit me to stay with them," Zephyr continued, her eyes flashing with electric blue light.

"They said connection was what drew me here, and like... yeah, maybe a little bit loosely. But really, it was curiosity. I followed a storm. I found a massive tempest hanging directly over the arena that refused to strike, and I couldn't figure out why the energy was held back. Then—bingo! Down the lightning came, and I was calling thunderbolts across the entire center ring!".

Ignatius's eyes went wide.

"Wait... were you the one striking the central copper obelisk?! Because that was a ton of lightning!".

Zephyr gave a coy, sly smirk.

"Who's to say? Could have been me... could have been anybody.".

"Okay, so that was definitely you," Ignatius laughed. He pointed to her trophy necklace.

"Do you keep a souvenir from everything you kill, or only the special ones?".

"Only the ones that aren't completely disintegrated by the lightning," Zephyr replied with a wicked grin, patting the raptor feather against her collar.

Chapter 7: No Such Thing As Luck

CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK.

The squad fell back into stride along the edge of the basin, marching steadily behind Mwaza-Kasa.

Bramble caught up to Aggie, his leafy branches rustling gently as he advocated for the weary cadets trailing behind them.

"I think... we will need to take a break here now," Bramble rumbled softly.

"Saffron, Pip, and I... we need food.".

The instant Bramble suggested breaking off, the Spirit Tortoise stopped dead in the sand. Its heavy limbs locked in place, and it turned its ancient neck around, fixing a stubborn, unblinking golden-teal stare directly upon them.

Aggie winced, looking back at Bramble and Pip with an apologetic grimace.

"Uh... I think you guys have to come with us," Aggie murmured hesitantly.

"I'm sorry.".

Pip threw her hands into the air, her voice exploding in an exhausted, exasperated wail.

"Yeah, no, see—here's the thing!"

Pip shouted, stomping her boot in the sand.

"I already wanted to leave at five in the morning! It wasn't worth it to me! There were snacks outside—I could have just hung out at the buffet tables the entire time! Aggie, I love you, you're one of my absolute favorites, but I am dealing with existentially not dying right now, so no!".

Aggie looked down at Mwaza-Kasa.

"Can they leave to get a snack and rejoin us later?"

Aggie asked gently.

The giant tortoise turned its ancient head, looked squarely at Aggie, and lifted its massive front foot.

STOMP. STOMP.

Two heavy, resonant thuds rattled the sand.

" I'm sorry, Pip.

" Aggie said with a sigh.

"The god tortoise says no. And I have a feeling this journey is really important—not just for my people, but for everyone.".

Pip slumped against Bramble's shoulder with a theatrical groan.

"Fine... you owe me snacks, dream turtle.".

Aggie unclipped the speaking stone from her belt, tapping the crystal surface.

"Britt... please tell me the walker has provisions.".

A sharp crackle answered from the stone as Professor Ink's poised voice resonated across the channel.

"Of course. Elijah is fully provisioned for an extended expedition into the forest.".

"I think we need more than just standard rations," Aggie said into the crystal.

"Pip is starving.".

Professor Ink paused, a hint of dry amusement in her tone.

"We have caramelized bacon in the galley.".

Pip's head snapped up like a hound catching a scent. Her eyes dilated with manic joy.

"Caramelized bacon?!"

Pip gasped.

"Let's go! Here we go!".

Without waiting for another word, the tiny pixie began power-walking toward the walker's coordinates, waving her arms back at the plant-kin.

"Brambies! Come on! Hurry up! We have to make sure there's enough for everyone!".

Meanwhile back at the walker Lomi informed Britt, "Hey, I need to double back into the medical tents for a few minutes. I saw Lucky earlier, and I have to check on him.".

"Go," Britt nodded.

"We'll meet at the rendezvous.".

Lomi jogged back through the crowded rows of canvas tents. He found Lucky exactly where he had seen him before—kneeling in the dirt beside a massive shape draped in heavy grey canvas, his head bowed and his broad shoulders shaking in silent, agonizing grief.

Lomi approached quietly, crouching beside his friend.

"Hey, Lucky. What's going on, man? What happened?".

Lucky didn't look up. His voice came out choked, muffled against his fists.

"I don't know, Lomi. I'm... I'm not feeling so lucky right now, man.".

Lomi placed a steady hand on Lucky's trembling shoulder.

"I know this was a brutal night. You lost a lot of good people. What's your plan now, Lucky? Where do you go from here?".

"I don't have a plan," Lucky choked out, wiping his eyes with a soot-covered sleeve.

"All the old dreams feel so stupid now. Like a kid's game. I was going to raid the world with Sarge... he wasn't supposed to leave me again. I wasn't supposed to get left behind again.".

Lomi looked at the shrouded body of Sarge, then met Lucky's hollow eyes.

"Here's the deal. We've got a crew. I don't really know what's going on, to be completely honest. I don't know how dangerous it's going to get, and I don't know what we're going to uncover in the forest. But I know one thing: I want you on board with us if you're able.".

"How?"

Lucky whispered, his voice cracking.

"How am I supposed to leave him behind?".

"I can't answer that for you, buddy," Lomi said softly.

"I know I'm older and wiser, but this is a grown-up moment. You have to make this choice for yourself.".

Lucky clenched his fists, fresh tears cutting through the grime on his cheeks.

"It was just a freak accident on the way out of the canyon. You build your whole life around this idea that you're untouchable... and then you realize it's always the people standing next to you who get hurt. What if I bring that curse to your crew, Lomi? What if I'm just bad luck?".

Lomi looked him dead in the eye and shook his head.

"There's no such thing as luck," Lomi said with utter conviction.

"I hate to break it to you, but there's no invisible force out there trying to balance the scales. There's just a magical giant tortoise that we have to follow.".

Lucky stared at him in complete disbelief, blinking away tears.

"What? Dude... that was a great speech right up until the last sentence, and then you lost me entirely.".

"I told you I don't know everything," Lomi chuckled, helping Lucky to his feet.

"We're searching for answers. That's what got me on board, and that might be enough for you. We're going to find out why this happened.".

Lucky took a ragged breath, looking down at Sarge's covered form.

"What would Sarge want done with his body, man? We never talked about it.".

"He was a simple man," Lomi replied warmly.

"What are you thinking?".

Lucky wiped his face, a faint spark returning to his bloodshot eyes.

"Yeah uh huh.. I think... I think I'm going to make old IronHide to shoot him out of the main deck cannon.".

Lomi blinkd in suprise, then laghing replied, "He would absolutely love that.".

"Where do I find your crew?"

Lucky asked, straightening his bruised shoulders.

"We're boarding a giant mechanical spider-walker at the north edge of camp," Lomi told him.

"Professor Ink has some of your gear stowed in the back. Take care of Sarge, and meet us there.".

"I'll be there," Lucky promised, turning with newfound resolve toward the command pavilion.

Chapter 8: The Ironclad Salute

CHAPTER 8: THE IRONCLAD SALUTE.

Lomi followed Lucky toward the command pavilion, where a circle of veteran officers stood near the harbor docks. At the center stood an imposing Goliath captain, completely bald, his face etched with ceremonial bridge-tattoos, wearing heavy iron plating riveted into a thick leather duster. Inscribed in polished brass across his chest armor was a single word: IRONCLAD.

Lucky approached the captain, his hand outstretched.

"Captain... it's about Sarge.".

The Goliath nodded with solemn gravity, placing a massive hand over Lucky's shoulder. He flagged down four of his strongest crewmen, who stepped forward with crisp military precision, lifted Sarge's shrouded stretcher onto their broad shoulders, and began an honor jog toward the colossal ironclad battleship moored at the central pier.

Lomi caught a passing dockworker by the sleeve.

"Hey, what time is it? It's like five in the morning, right?".

The worker glanced at the high morning glare.

"It's almost noon, mate. The night storm ate three hours of daylight.".

"Oh right...got it," Lomi nodded, picking up his pace.

"Whatever, I've got time to see this through."

Smiling, Lomi jied the procession toward the Ironclad to see Sarge off.

Lomi wasn't the only one to make use of the hour before the crew was set to depart. Across the thinning triage rows, Aggie doubled back to find Val sitting beside Kale's cot. The heavy canvas tarps had been cleared away, leaving Val staring silently into the distance.

Val looked up as Aggie approached. Aggie - seeing the hurt in Val's eyes forged ahead with the short speech she had been rehearsing in her head, "Look... I'm sorry. I don't know what to say in a moment like this. And I don't know the why of what happened here. But I think we're going to find out why. We have a connection with our Spirit Tortoise, and it's leading us somewhere.".

Val took a moment before responding, his voice quiet and heavy.

"There's been a theory spreading through the camp that my father broke the resonance grid when he first discovered your clan's valley," Val murmured, his fists resting on his knees.

"I don't know the truth behind any of it. But if your spirit tortoise is moving...

is there a chance to set that right?".

"I hope so," Aggie said gently.

"Whether or not your father was the cause, we need to find the truth.".

Val looked at Kale, who gave him a firm, supportive nod. Val stood up, extending a hand to clasp Aggie's.

"Then I want to come with you. Lead the way.".

The two quickly caught back up with Ignatious who was standing guard at the renedezvous point - mostly making sure Pip didn't run off for snacks before the walker could arrive.

Suddenly, a deafening thunderclap ripped across the entire basin.

BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! Back across the camp, With his front row seat from the deck of the Ironclad, Lomi watched as a full naval broadside erupted from the massive turrets of the Ironclad battleship. The colossal artillery shells detonated in mid-air over the turquoise water, unleashing a dense, rolling thundercloud of black gunpowder smoke across the bay. A second synchronized barrage fired immediately after, igniting the smoke cloud from within with brilliant resonance pyrotechnics that painted the morning sky in vibrant streaks of crimson, gold, and turquoise.

A third salvo cracked like lightning, instantly dispelling the storm cloud in a breathtaking twenty-one-gun salute as Sarge's body was committed to the deep canyon waters.

Soon after, Lucky stepped away from the battleship's gangway and jogged up beside Lomi on the beach, his jaw set with fierce resolve.

"All right," Lucky said, rolling his shoulders.

"I don't know what we're walking into, but I'm ready. Let's do this. Let's go.".

"Let's do it," Lomi smiled.

They sprinted across the sand to where Elijah, Professor Ink's four-legged spider-walker, now stood idling at the forest perimeter.

The entire expedition gathered at the base ladder: Britt, Iggy, Ignatius, Lomi, Aggie, Val, Pip, Bramble, Saffron, Zephyr, and Lucky—six extra companions in total. One by one, they scrambled up the iron rungs into the hull.

As the lower entry hatch sealed shut with a pressurized hiss, the massive Spirit Tortoise looked up, met Aggie's eyes through the observation glass with a solemn nod, and surged forward—spinning a trail of flattened brush behind it as Elijah's mechanical legs kicked into a galloping sprint, racing straight across the plains towards the ancient Mizizi forest.

Chapter 9: The Lab Below

CHAPTER 9: THE LAB BELOW.

Inside the humming hull of the four-legged walker Elijah, the machine settled into a rhythmic, lurching gallop across the savanna grasslands.

The main operations compartment opened into a spacious central lounge arranged around a long tactical table. Projecting from the center was an acoustic holographic display showing the vast terrain stretching between Vumbua and the distant Mizizi forest, with a plotted route cutting across the flat plains.

While the squad traded quick pleasantries and claimed bunks, Rill stepped over to where Zephyr was lounging near Ignatius, nodding stiffly at the tempest cadet.

"I'm glad you're alive," Rill muttered—a courtesy delivered with visible reservation.

Then Rill's gaze shifted to Britt, and the color instantly drained from her face. She gasped, slapping a hand against her forehead.

"Oh gods... I completely forgot!"

Rill exclaimed in sudden panic. She grabbed Britt's forearm with urgent force.

"Britt, I need you down in the lower laboratory right now! This very second—fast as you can move!".

Without waiting for an answer, Rill sprinted across the deck, threw open the floor hatch, and slid down the ladder rungs like a drop of water down a conduit pipe.

Britt hurried after her without hesitation, with Aggie dropping through the hatch right behind them. Iggy hovered by the ladder, eyeing Zephyr suspiciously; but seeing the purple-haired cadet cross her boots and lean back for a nap, he decided she wasn't going anywhere. Iggy made a quick, theatrical warding gesture with his soil-stained fingers—a cheeky half-hex to keep her asleep—and scrambled down the ladder after the squad. Ignatius trailed down last, feeling distinctly awkward in the confined research bay.

Down in the lower laboratory, Rill rushed to a heavy, reinforced containment safe mounted in the corner. She spun the combination dials, threw back the steel latch, and retrieved a small glass vial filled with a luminous, swirling neon liquid.

The glowing fluid inside was the exact iridescent hue as the mysterious substance Britt had discovered in the buried cache where they had recovered the compass.

Rill turned around, holding the vial up to the light.

"Britt... does this liquid look familiar to you?".

Britt stared at the shimmering contents, her pulse spiking.

"Yeah," Britt said grimly.

"That looks identical to the substance that caused the fungal rash spreading on my shoulder.".

"Not good," Rill muttered, her voice trembling as she gestured frantically toward an examination stool.

"Not good at all! Sit down, please—sit down right now!".

Rill reached into her medical kit and pulled out a second glass vial, this one filled with a dense, shimmering neon-purple tonic. She shoved it into Britt's hands.

"Drink this immediately," Rill commanded urgently.

"What is this?"

Britt asked, looking down at the purple draught.

Rill took a deep, shaky breath, leaning against the lab counter.

"I was in Professor Ink's laboratory when the field sample was brought in from the ruins. It completely gutted me to recognize it... because this substance comes from the canyon territory where I was raised. Back before the clan exchange that I still can't talk about.".

Rill pointed at the glowing vial, her eyes wide with terror.

"You were exposed to a lethal biological agent that grows in only one isolated canyon gorge. It has a permanent cure, but I can't rememebr exactly how to make it and I wouldn't have what I'd need here anyway. But if you drink this stabilizing tonic once every seven days, it halts the cellular degradation. Because if you don't drink this, Britt... you are going to die in about two weeks.".

Britt stared down at the vial, the weight of the diagnosis pressing heavily into her chest. The memory of the ancient vision that the Mwaza Kassa had shown her in the branches of the Arena echoed in her mind—she had seen others suffering from this same wasting illness in the memories of the old world, people who had asked dangerous questions and left the forest canopy.

"Has this substance ever come into contact with the Mizizi clan before?"

Britt asked carefully.

"That should be impossible," Rill answered, shaking her head vigorously.

"It grows in only one forbidden canyon cave, and no one ever goes there!".

"I think I carry memories of our people struggling with this exact condition," Britt pressed, her green eyes boring into Rill's.

"Not necessarily the liquid itself, but the illness it causes.".

Rill stared at her, baffled.

"That makes no sense at all. It shouldn't be inside the Mizizi forest. Why would it be here? Why would it do the exact same thing to you that it does to the canyon folk?!".

"Where does it come from?"

Britt asked.

"Was it manufactured, or does it grow naturally?".

"It isn't manufactured," Rill whispered.

"It just grows.".

Rill stepped over to the laboratory door, slid the heavy iron deadbolt shut, and turned to face the room. Only the four of them remained inside: Rill, Britt, Aggie, and Iggy, with Ignatius standing quietly near the ladder rungs.

Chapter 10: Wadi Water

CHAPTER 10: WADI WATER.

In the quiet of the locked laboratory, Rill leaned back against the steel door, wrapping her arms tightly around herself.

"I've been keeping this inside for so long," Rill confessed softly, looking between Britt, Aggie, and Iggy.

"It's just so hard to talk about where I came from... the clan exchange scrubbed so much out of us, and I'm still trying to overcome that indoctrination every day. But I want to be honest with you.".

She took a deep breath, her electric-blue hair falling across her brow.

"I'm originally from a clan that called themselves the Wadi. We lived in the deep western canyon. Our ancestral spark—the thing that made our people special—was a sacred source of water. But for my entire childhood, the spring was dead. Just a few dry drips and trickles. We thought our entire civilization was dying out.".

Ignatius stepped closer, his eyes wide with recognition.

"That's just like the Ash-Blood clan," Ignatius whispered.

"Our magma springs went cold... we thought our whole people were going to go under.".

"Yes," Rill nodded, her voice thick with emotion.

"It was the exact same thing. When I was chosen for the exchange, I left not even knowing if my family would survive. But in our canyon, there was a deep, hidden cave—one of the only places that stayed damp through the worst droughts. And that cave was where this glowing fungus grew. It needed that spring and should not have been able to grow anywhere else in the world. So for you to say that you've seen people suffering from these symptoms in the Mizizi forest... the only explanation is that something connected our lands in the ancient before-times.".

"The old turtles," Ignatius suggested.

"The ancient network.".

"Maybe," Rill murmured.

"I was never trusted with the deepest clan secrets because I was new. But I traveled through the mycelium network once... and it was terrifying.".

"That's how we survived the arena storm!"

Ignatius said proudly.

"Thanks to Britt and Aggie speaking to the roots, we didn't die in the forest.".

Aggie chimed in shaking her head.

"Talking to trees is different. There's the fungal network, which speaks to the living flora, and then there's the deep mycelium network, which carries the soul and allows physical travel across the network.".

Rill turned back to the lab counter, flipping through stacks of parchment charts and botanical sketches. She pointed to a glass terrarium holding three small field mice, each showing the same distinct grey fungal decay along their spines.

"I don't love animal testing," Rill admitted quietly, "but when I realized what was happening to you, Britt, I panicked. I worked with Professor Ink using Harmony compounds to synthesize this stabilizer. This isn't natural to the forest. Someone brought it here.".

Britt crossed her arms, her jaw tightening.

"This substance wasn't found in the deep woods. I was infected right after we arrived in Harmony, down in a drainage ditch near the cliffside where we found an old cache containing a ten-year-old compass.".

Rill went rigid.

"A ten-year-old cache?! Has anyone else in your clan ever died from this condition?".

"Yes," Britt answered.

"I can sort of remember... about ten people. Adventurers who left the forest to explore the outer world.".

A chill settled over the room.

"Ten people," Rill whispered.

"All curious wanderers who left the forest... dying of a poison that exists in only one isolated canyon gorge.".

Ignatius looked between them, scratching his head.

"Wait... isn't dying supposed to be considered a natural, good thing in your clan philosophy?".

"Ignatius, read the room!"

Rill hissed.

"We are on an active investigation!".

"No, think about it!"

Ignatius insisted, stepping forward.

"My people were dying out, then we connected with Harmony, and suddenly our magma erupted with life! Your clan revered death and balance, and now that you've connected with Harmony, you're finding more death and disease! Doesn't the timeline seem suspicious?".

"We do not worship death," Brittt corrected fiercely.

"We acknowledge that death is an inevitable truth of the world, and that balance between growth and decay must be respected. But the last time this illness appeared among the Mizizi was ten years ago—long before Captain Vane ever discovered our valley, and long before the Harmony cartographers arrived!".

"Which means there is a third, unknown variable at play," Ignatius concluded.

"Exactly," Rill said. She picked up the neon-purple vial, pressing it gently into Britt's hands.

"I don't have all the answers yet, Britt. But I know for a fact that if you don't drink this, you won't survive the fortnight.".

Britt hesitated, staring down at the swirling tonic.

"Intervening like this... it feels like interrupting the natural path. Is this supposed to happen?".

Ignatius placed a warm, steady hand on Britt's shoulder, his voice dropping to a sincere, earnest cadence.

"Britt, hear me out," Ignatius said gently.

"This isn't an interruption of nature. This medicine was made from natural waters, synthesized so that you can stay alive and save your people. You are a core part of this squad. We need you for whatever is coming next. Nobody in this room wants to watch you die—and I genuinely do not believe it is your time to go.".

Britt looked up, meeting Ignatius's warm, fiery eyes, then glanced at Aggie and Iggy's supportive faces.

"That's not for you to decide," Britt murmured softly.

"You're right," Ignatius smiled warmly.

"It's for you to decide.".

Britt nodded. Without another word, she popped the cork, tipped the glass vial back, and drank the shimmering purple tonic in a single long gulp.

Rill held her breath, leaning forward.

"How does it taste?".

Britt smacked her lips, blinking in surprise.

"It... honestly tastes like Gatorade.".

"Gatorade!"

Rill laughed with overwhelming relief, slumping against the counter.

"Thank the Water."

She wiped a bead of sweat from her forehead and smiled.

"Okay. Now... onto the next problem.".

Chapter 11: The Heartbeat In The Grass

CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS.

Back up in the operations room, instead of following the squad into the lab, Lomi had ambled toward the iron spiral staircase leading up to the open-air observation bridge, eager to take in his very first sight of the world beyond the city walls.

High atop the walker Elijah, the open observation bridge was constructed from polished bamboo struts, brass instrumentation, and reinforced glass.

From this elevated vantage, the world unfolded into an endless, emerald expanse of rolling savanna grassland.

Far to the south, smudged against the pale morning horizon, the dark, colossal wall of the ancient Mizizi forest stretched for eighty miles—only the outer perimeter of their true destination.

Up in the pilot's cradle at the forward helm sat a small, sharp-featured goblin driver, his clawed hands flicking brass toggle switches with bored, practiced efficiency. Standing beside the navigation console was Professor Ink, her sharp eyes studying the distant horizon.

Ambling over to the helm with an easy mechanic's slouch, Lomi leaned on the brass railing.

"So... how hard is a beauty like this to drive?"
